title: Vichyssoise
subtitle: Chilled French leek and potato soup
excerpt: A silky, chilled French soup of leeks and potatoes blended with cream and served cold with a scattering of chives. Elegant, simple, and better made the day before.

recipe.sourceNotes: Vichyssoise was created in 1917 by French chef Louis Diat at the Ritz-Carlton Hotel in New York. Diat developed the soup based on the cold leek and potato soup he remembered his mother and grandmother making in Vichy in central France, chilling and enriching it with cream for the hotel's fashionable clientele. Despite being a French-American creation, its name (meaning 'from Vichy') gives it a French character. The key to its distinctive silk texture is blending thoroughly until completely smooth and then passing through a fine sieve. Vichyssoise is always served cold: it can be made hot as a leek and potato soup, but the cold version is a completely different experience.

recipeTools.notes: A large saucepan and a blender or stick blender.

content.text: Use only the white and pale green parts of the leek; the dark green parts are too fibrous and will colour the soup. Blend thoroughly: the smoothness of the final soup depends on this. Pass through a fine sieve after blending for the silkiest result. Chill for at least 4 hours before serving; the soup thickens as it cools, so it may need a splash of cold stock to adjust consistency before serving.

items.preparation: white and pale green parts only, cleaned and sliced

content.text: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the leeks and onion and cook gently for 15 minutes until completely soft but not coloured.
Add the potatoes, stock, bay leaves, and salt. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender. Remove the bay leaves.

Blend thoroughly until completely smooth. Pass through a fine sieve into a clean bowl. Stir in the cream. Season with salt and white pepper. Cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight. Adjust consistency with a little cold stock if needed. Serve in chilled bowls with a drizzle of cream and a scattering of chives.
